Location: Bay St. Louis, Biloxi (Back Bay), Pascagoula (MS); Mobile & Saraland (AL) – CSX railroad drawbridges
Item: Proposed rule: 5 CSX rail drawbridges to be run remotely from Mobile
Details: Coast Guard proposed rule (published Oct 7, 2026) would let CSX operate five railroad drawbridges remotely from a yard in Mobile instead of with on-site tenders: Bay St. Louis (mile 0.5, 13 ft closed clearance), Back Bay of Biloxi (mile 0.4, 14 ft), Pascagoula River (mile 1.5, 8 ft), Three Mile Creek (mile 0.0, 3 ft) and Chickasaw Creek (mile 0.0, 7 ft). Bridges would still open on signal; rule requires them to stay open if cameras, communications or visibility fail.
When: Proposed Oct 7 2026; public comments due Nov 6 2026; final rule date not set
Notes: No change to opening schedule yet – this is a proposal. Covers MS and AL; map point is Bay St. Louis town center as a representative location. End date = comment deadline. Coast Guard contact: Douglas Blakemore 504-671-2127.

Location: Schooner Bayou Control Structure, Vermilion Parish (Mermentau Basin, GIWW)
Item: Schooner Bayou on restricted locking – low water and high salinity
Details: Corps of Engineers Navigation Bulletin 26-100: since 6am Oct 5 the structure locks only every 2 hours on the even hours, 6am–6pm daily, and only outboards and light vessels are being locked through; all tows are sent to Leland Bowman Lock. Why it matters: a timed, size-limited locking can turn an assumed passage into a long wait or a reroute – sailboats and heavier cruisers shouldn't assume 'light vessels' includes them.
Notes: What to do: call Lockmaster Casey Choate at 337-737-2470 or 337-316-3662 before committing to this route; if your boat doesn't qualify, plan around via Leland Bowman Lock. Corps New Orleans District contact: Michael Sullivan 504-862-2373. 'Light vessels' is not defined in the bulletin.

Location: Harvey Lock, Harvey (GIWW west of New Orleans, Harvey Canal / Mississippi River)
Item: Harvey Lock reopened – normal operations resumed
Details: Corps of Engineers Navigation Bulletin 26-99 (Oct 5): Harvey Lock is open to navigation and back to normal operations. It had been closed since Sept 9 because low Mississippi River stages created a reverse-head risk to the lock gates. Why it matters: Harvey is one of the key links between the GIWW and the Mississippi on the west side of New Orleans – this removes a routing complication that's been in place for almost a month.
Notes: What to do: Harvey Lock can go back into route plans. The Corps still recommends checking status with Lockmaster Greg Desselles (504-366-4683; lock wall 504-366-5187) before arrival. River stages are still low, so a repeat closure is possible if the river drops again.
